ja: 引っ越しで一番きつかったのは、知り合いがいないこと。
en: What was toughest about moving was not knowing anyone.
alternatives: The toughest part of moving was not knowing a soul.
The hardest thing about moving was not knowing anyone.
point: What was toughest で主語を作り、was の後に動名詞

ja: 最近、週末は何をしてるの？
en: What do you do weekends these days?
alternatives: How do you spend weekends these days?
What do you usually do on weekends?
point: 習慣は現在形 do。「最近」は these days

ja: 君が入院してたなんて、全然知らなかったよ。
en: Little did I know you'd been in the hospital.
alternatives: I had no idea you'd been in the hospital.
I never knew you'd been in the hospital.
point: Little を文頭に置くと did I know の語順になる

ja: 私、ここ数年で今が一番忙しいよ。
en: This is the busiest I've been in years.
alternatives: I haven't been this busy in years.
I'm busier now than I've been in years.
point: 最上級のあとは I've been と現在完了で続ける

ja: 姉は夏中、ホステルに泊まって旅してたよ。
en: My sister traveled all summer, staying in hostels.
alternatives: My sister spent all summer traveling, staying in hostels.
My sister traveled all summer and stayed in hostels.
point: 「泊まって」は , staying と分詞で後ろにつなげる

ja: ケンが、来月大阪に転勤になるって言ってたよ。
en: Ken said he's being transferred to Osaka next month.
alternatives: Ken told me he'd be transferred to Osaka next month.
Ken mentioned he's being transferred to Osaka next month.
point: 転勤「になる」は受動態 be transferred

ja: ずっと君に連絡しなきゃと思ってたんだ。
en: I've been meaning to get in touch with you.
alternatives: I've been meaning to reach out to you.
I've been meaning to contact you.
point: 「〜しようと思ってた」は been meaning to + 動詞

ja: 君が農業を始めるって聞いて、驚いたのは決断の早さだよ。
en: What surprised me was how fast you decided to farm.
alternatives: What shocked me was how quickly you decided to farm.
I was surprised by how fast you decided to go into farming.
point: 「驚いたのは〜だった」は What surprised me was で組み立てる

ja: 昨日君が会った人、僕のいとこなんだ。
en: The man you met yesterday is my cousin.
alternatives: The guy you met yesterday is my cousin.
The person you met yesterday is my cousin.
point: 会った人は the man (that) you met と後ろから説明

ja: 戻ってきたら、みんなで集まろうよ。
en: When you're back, let's all get together.
alternatives: Once you're back, let's get everyone together.
Let's all meet up when you get back.
point: 未来のことでも when 節は現在形で言う

ja: 仕事が忙しくて、ほとんど時間がないよ。
en: Work's been crazy; I barely have time.
alternatives: I've been swamped, so I hardly have time.
Work's been busy, so I hardly have time.
point: 「ほとんどない」は hardly / barely で、not を重ねない

ja: 兄、最近よく英語やっとけばよかったって言うんだ。
en: My brother keeps saying he wishes he'd studied English.
alternatives: My brother often says he wishes he'd studied English.
My brother keeps saying he should've studied English.
point: 過去を悔やむ wish の後は had + 過去分詞

ja: 留学中の妹は、いい助言をもらってるらしいよ。
en: Apparently, my sister abroad is getting some good advice.
alternatives: I hear my sister abroad is getting some good advice.
My sister who's studying abroad is apparently getting good advice.
point: advice は数えられない名詞。advices にしない

ja: 去年二人でキャンプを始めて、すっかりハマってるよ。
en: We took up camping last year, and we're hooked.
alternatives: We started camping last year, and we're really into it.
We got into camping last year, and we love it.
point: 「ハマっている」は今の状態なので現在形で言う

ja: 私が君の立場なら、燃え尽きてるだろうな。
en: If I were in your shoes, I'd be burned out.
alternatives: If I were you, I'd be burned out.
I'd be completely burned out if I were in your shoes.
point: 仮定は were、結果は would＋動詞の原形

ja: 兄は今、カナダで英語を勉強中。
en: My brother's studying English in Canada.
alternatives: He's studying English in Canada.
My brother's in Canada studying English.
point: 今していることは is と動詞の ing 形で言う

ja: あのとき留学してたら、今ごろ英語ペラペラなのに。
en: If I'd studied abroad then, I'd be fluent now.
alternatives: If I'd studied abroad back then, I'd be fluent now.
If I'd studied abroad then, I'd be fluent by now.
point: 過去の仮定は had+過去分詞、今の結果は would+動詞の原形

ja: 仕事は忙しいけど、最近料理教室に通ってるよ。
en: Work's busy, but I've been taking a cooking class.
alternatives: Although work is busy, I've been going to cooking classes.
Work's hectic, but lately I've been taking a cooking class.
point: 続いている習慣は現在完了進行形 I've been taking

ja: 今度、電話してもいい？
en: May I call you sometime?
alternatives: Can I call you sometime?
Is it okay to call you sometime?
point: 許可を求めるときは May I / Can I。「今度」は sometime

ja: 海外に住んでる友達に会ったよ。
en: I saw a friend who lives abroad.
alternatives: I met a friend who lives overseas.
I saw a friend that lives abroad.
point: 人を後ろから who 節で説明する。who の後ろは動詞

ja: 引っ越しのこと、もっと早く言うべきだったね。
en: I should've told you about the move sooner.
alternatives: I should have told you about the move earlier.
I should've mentioned the move sooner.
point: 「すべきだったのに」は should have + 過去分詞

ja: 私、今はギターが弾けるよ。
en: I can play the guitar now.
alternatives: Now I can play the guitar.
I can play guitar now.
point: 楽器は play the guitar。「弾ける」は can＋動詞

ja: 彼女、最近ギターにはまってるらしいよ。
en: I hear she's into playing guitar lately.
alternatives: Apparently she's hooked on playing guitar lately.
I heard she's really into playing guitar now.
point: 前置詞 into の後ろは動名詞 playing

ja: 隣の人、結婚したらしいよ。
en: I hear the guy next door tied the knot.
alternatives: Apparently the man next door got married.
I heard the guy next door got married.
point: 「隣の人」は the guy next door と名詞の後ろに置く

ja: 兄に手伝ってと頼まれたんだ。
en: My brother asked me to help.
alternatives: My brother asked for my help.
My brother asked me for help.
point: ask + 人 + to do の形。me を忘れずに

ja: 君が電話くれなかったら、今も落ち込んでたよ。
en: If you hadn't called, I'd still be moping around.
alternatives: If you hadn't called me, I'd still be feeling down.
Without your call, I'd still be down.
point: 過去の仮定＋今への影響は If 過去完了, would be

ja: 先月引っ越して、まだ荷ほどき中だよ。
en: I moved last month; I'm still unpacking.
alternatives: I moved last month and still haven't unpacked.
Last month I moved, and I'm still unpacking.
point: 過去の出来事は moved、今も続く状態は現在進行形で言い分ける

ja: たしか、ユミは先月昇進したはずだよ。
en: If I remember right, Yumi got promoted last month.
alternatives: Yumi got promoted last month, if I remember right.
As far as I remember, Yumi was promoted last month.
point: 自信のない記憶は If I remember right で和らげる

ja: 先月やっと、キッチンをリフォームしてもらったんだ。
en: I finally had my kitchen remodeled last month.
alternatives: I finally got my kitchen remodeled last month.
Last month, I finally got the kitchen redone.
point: 「〜してもらう」は have / get + 物 + 過去分詞

ja: 最近何してるのか教えてよ。
en: Tell me what you've been up to.
alternatives: Let me know what you've been up to.
Tell me what you've been doing lately.
point: what 以下は疑問文の語順にせず、what you've been の順にする

ja: 疲れてるね。もっと寝たほうがいいよ。
en: You look tired. You should sleep more.
alternatives: You look tired. You need more sleep.
You look tired. Try to sleep more.
point: 「〜したほうがいい」は should＋動詞の原形

ja: 学生時代に知り合った人と、今も会ってる？
en: Do you still see anyone you knew in school?
alternatives: Are you still in touch with anyone from school?
Do you still see anyone from your school days?
point: anyone のあとに you knew を続けて説明する
